# Model 11 (Optimized Ensemble)

Introduced into HistGradientBoostingRegressor in this model is learning_rate, and max_iter was increased to refine the model's accuracy on the final spend predictions.

```{python}
#| warning: false

import pandas as pd
from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingRegressor

data = pd.read_csv('../PACFiles/analysis_data.csv')
X = pd.get_dummies(data.drop(['customer_id', 'monthly_spend'], axis=1), drop_first=True)
y = data.monthly_spend

model = HistGradientBoostingRegressor(max_iter=500, learning_rate=0.03, random_state=617)
model.fit(X,y)

scoring_data = pd.read_csv('../PACFiles/scoring_data.csv')
scoring_X = pd.get_dummies(scoring_data.drop(['customer_id'], axis=1), drop_first=True)
scoring_X = scoring_X.reindex(columns=X.columns, fill_value=0)
pred = model.predict(scoring_X)

submission_file = pd.DataFrame({'customer_id': scoring_data.customer_id, 'monthly_spend': pred})
submission_file.to_csv('../PACFiles/submission_file_12.csv', index=False)

from sklearn.metrics import root_mean_squared_error
train_pred = model.predict(X)
rmse = root_mean_squared_error(y, train_pred)
print("Training RMSE:", rmse)
```
